title: Countering-China spending has scale without a complete portfolio evidence system
source_unit: GAO review of State and USAID countering-Chinese-influence projects and interagency funding processes, fiscal years 2020-2023
geography: United States foreign-assistance programs and global project portfolio

observations.period: Fiscal years 2020-2023; GAO review published June 2026

denominator.unit: estimated funded projects in State and USAID countering-Chinese-influence portfolio

results_framework.value: no portfolio-wide assessment process; framework development remained uncertain as of March 2026

observations.method: GAO reviewed agency guidance, project data, documents, interviews with officials, and the development status of a monitoring, evaluation, and learning framework. Aggregate project counts and allocations were judged sufficiently reliable for reporting, while project-level completeness and effectiveness evidence were not.
observations.uncertainty: The source identifies data and evaluation gaps; it does not prove that individual projects were ineffective or that countering influence had no effects. The latest project data analyzed were for fiscal years 2020-2023.
observations.subgroup: State and USAID bureaus, overseas posts, regions, and projects funded through CCIF/CPRCIF-related accounts.
observations.counterinterpretation: A fragmented portfolio can still contain effective projects; missing standardized evaluation may reflect program design, security sensitivity, or administrative transition rather than failure of every intervention.

boundary: This record shows a state-capacity and evidence-governance problem inside a geopolitical competition program: funding scale and proposal activity are more visible than complete project identity, implementation status, and results. It does not estimate Chinese influence, project effectiveness, recipient-country behavior, or strategic outcomes.
